subject: Computer Networking
title: Social Networks Emerge
description: A 60-second lesson on Social Networks Emerge.

hook.text: Friendster in 2002, MySpace in 2003, Facebook in 2004 — the web became a place to connect with people.

buildup.text: Social networks needed always-on broadband, photo uploads, and dynamic pages. Earlier internet couldn't support them.

discovery.text: Facebook scaled from a dorm project to a billion users by building one of the world's largest data center networks.

twist.text: Social networks made users the content. The business model was selling attention, not selling products.

climax.text: By 2010, social media was reshaping politics, journalism, and culture. Networking wasn't just technical anymore.

punchline.text: Social networks turned the internet into a mirror of society.

quiz.question: What infrastructure enabled social networks to scale globally?
options: Massive data center networks and broadband adoption

details.summary: Social networking evolved from early platforms like Friendster and MySpace to Facebook's launch in 2004 and Twitter in 2006. These platforms transformed the internet from a content consumption medium into a participatory communication platform where billions create and share content daily.
details.whyItMatters: Social networks transformed human communication and information sharing. They made every person a publisher and fundamentally changed politics, business, and culture.
takeaways: Friendster and MySpace pioneered social networking in the early 2000s
Facebook scaled to billions by focusing on real identity
Social platforms transformed users from consumers to creators

faq.question: Why did Facebook succeed where earlier networks failed?
faq.answer: Facebook required real names and started with a trusted college community, creating an authentic social graph. It expanded carefully, maintaining quality. Its platform model let developers build on top of it. Scale effects made it increasingly valuable as more people joined.

faq.question: How did social networks change the internet?
faq.answer: They shifted the internet from websites publishing to users to users publishing to each other. Content creation became democratic. News distribution shifted from editors to algorithms. Social networks became the primary way billions of people experience the internet daily.
